boulder/0.title: November ballot measures
boulder/0.summary: Council put several questions on the November 3 ballot, including general obligation bonds for recreation and safety projects, a vacancy excise tax on homes occupied 183 days a year or less, a charter right for firefighters to bargain collectively, and a wildfire resilience measure for open space.

boulder/1.title: Boulder Downtown Development Authority
boulder/1.summary: Council moved to ask downtown voters whether to form a Downtown Development Authority that could use tax increment financing for downtown projects.

boulder/2.title: Wildfire resilience and home hardening
boulder/2.summary: Council worked on a wildfire home hardening hub and a review of every city wildfire program as a council priority project, alongside the open space wildfire ballot measure.

boulder/3.title: Local minimum wage increase
boulder/3.summary: Council held the second reading of an ordinance setting Boulder's local minimum wage.

boulder/4.title: 2027 budget
boulder/4.summary: Council held a study session on the 2027 recommended budget and then adopted budgets and mill levies for the downtown, University Hill and Boulder Junction improvement districts.
boulder/4.where: Citywide, Downtown, University Hill, Boulder Junction

boulder/5.title: Eminent domain for the 30th Street projects
boulder/5.summary: Council introduced ordinances allowing the city to buy or condemn land for the North 30th Street project and the South 30th Street multimodal improvements.

boulder/6.title: Annexation of Cherryvale Road and McSorley Lane properties
boulder/6.summary: Council took up a petition to annex about 5.4 acres at 1275 Cherryvale Rd. and 5995 McSorley Ln. with rural residential zoning, setting a public hearing for November 12.

boulder/7.title: Affordable housing bonds for Boulder Housing Partners and Harvest34
boulder/7.summary: Council assigned $7.3 million in private activity bonds to Boulder Housing Partners for permanently affordable rentals and cleared housing revenue bonds for the Harvest34 project.

boulder/8.title: Arapahoe Avenue rezoning and Naropa campus redevelopment
boulder/8.summary: Council introduced a rezoning of 3.7 acres at 2106 and 2130 Arapahoe Avenue to high-density residential, vacated part of Marine Street, and reviewed a site plan to redevelop the Naropa campus.

boulder/9.title: Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan update
boulder/9.summary: Council introduced the ordinance adopting the 2025 major ten-year update to the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan.

boulder/10.title: Power reliability and resilience forum
boulder/10.summary: Council held a community forum on power reliability and resilience, a council priority project, and reviewed a concept plan to expand Xcel Energy's service center at 2655 N. 63rd Street.

boulder/11.title: Civic Area East Bookend redevelopment
boulder/11.summary: Council discussed a request for proposals for a development partner on the east end of the Civic Area.

boulder/12.title: Marijuana and liquor licensing changes
boulder/12.summary: Council updated the medical and recreational marijuana code and created expanded permits and a tax for spirits manufacturers.

boulder/13.title: Pedicab licenses
boulder/13.summary: Council created licenses and fees for pedicab companies and drivers.

boulder/14.title: Frasier senior campus expansion
boulder/14.summary: Council reviewed a site review amendment for Frasier to build a 55-foot, four-story, 96-unit independent living building with underground parking.

boulder/15.title: Landmark designations at 1004 Lincoln Place and 844-850 12th Street
boulder/15.summary: Council designated two properties as individual landmarks.

denver/0.title: Data center moratorium
denver/0.summary: City staff updated the Community Planning and Housing committee on Denver's moratorium on new data centers while the city works out rules for where they can go and how much power and water they can use.

denver/1.title: NWSL stadium at Santa Fe Yards and the Broadway Station bridge
denver/1.summary: Council amended the agreement with the Broadway Station metro district for the women's pro soccer stadium site and took a state grant for a pedestrian bridge over the rail lines linking the Broadway RTD station to the stadium and Santa Fe Yards.

denver/2.title: Mayor's proposed 2027 budget
denver/2.summary: The Finance Department walked council through the budget book, council worked through proposed changes to sales tax initiatives, and the mayor's 2027 budget was set for a public hearing on October 26.

sources.body: Operations Meeting of the City Council

denver/3.title: Denver Health sales tax spending
denver/3.summary: Council reviewed how the 0.34% Denver Health sales tax approved in 2024 is being spent and moved a string of new and amended contracts with Denver Health, including the behavioral health services at 777 Bannock Street.

denver/4.title: Homeless shelters and rapid rehousing contracts
denver/4.summary: Council approved a run of contracts for rapid resolution and rehousing, new emergency shelter at the Sand & Sage/Westerner Motel on East Colfax, a safe outdoor space at 3815 N Steele Street and a micro-community shelter site.
denver/4.where: Sand & Sage Motel (East Colfax), 3815 N Steele St

denver/5.title: Downtown Development Authority boundaries and projects
denver/5.summary: Council repeatedly expanded the Denver Downtown Development Authority's boundaries and approved DDA funding for the Midland Condominiums, the University Building on 16th Street and 101 W Colfax, where the city is also leasing space.

denver/6.title: Council votes down Citibot and Slalom tech contracts
denver/6.summary: After being called out for debate, resolutions adding $3.9 million to the Citibot chatbot contract and $5 million to the Slalom consulting contract both failed on the council floor.

denver/7.title: Sunny Side Up city video contract
denver/7.summary: A contract for city marketing and recruiting videos drew pushback; an added $600,000 failed on the floor in August before a smaller $250,000 amendment came back in the fall.

denver/8.title: Affordable housing bonds and loans
denver/8.summary: Council approved housing revenue bonds for the Green Valley Vistas and Link and Pin apartments, a loan for 1600 Pearl, a loan for a 118-unit income-restricted building, and state money for middle-income row homes at Loretto Heights.
denver/8.where: Green Valley Ranch, North Capitol Hill, Loretto Heights

denver/9.title: Universal Recycling and Composting Ordinance rollout
denver/9.summary: Council heard an update on putting the recycling and composting ordinance into effect, which phases in recycling and compost service requirements for apartments and businesses.

denver/10.title: Flood control at the Globeville Levee, Sanderson Gulch and Harvard Gulch
denver/10.summary: Council moved agreements with the Mile High Flood District and federal grants for drainage and flood control work on the Globeville Levee from 31st Street to East 50th Avenue, along Sanderson Gulch and at Harvard Gulch.
denver/10.where: Globeville Levee, Sanderson Gulch, Harvard Gulch

denver/11.title: Airport expansion and airline leases at DIA
denver/11.summary: Council approved a $135 million project management contract for the North Terminal expansion, taxiway and gate apron construction, and new use-and-lease agreements with ten airlines.

denver/12.title: Rewrite of the city's minority and women-owned business contracting rules
denver/12.summary: Council passed a rewrite of the city code's minority-owned, women-owned and small business enterprise contracting program.

denver/13.title: Housing Stability's one-year plan for 2027
denver/13.summary: Council changed the code so the Department of Housing Stability can run on a one-year continuation plan for 2027 and bring a new long-range strategic plan in September 2027.

denver/14.title: Missing middle housing and zoning reform
denver/14.summary: Council toured missing middle housing as part of Unlocking Housing Choices and heard about regulatory reform and a federal PRO Housing grant meant to make more kinds of homes legal to build.

denver/15.title: West Colfax and Hazel Court rezonings
denver/15.summary: Council moved rezonings at 3418 W 14th Avenue and 1371 N Julian Street in West Colfax and held a public hearing on rezoning 76 N Hazel Court and nearby lots.
denver/15.where: 3418 W 14th Ave, 1371 N Julian St, 76 N Hazel Ct

denver/16.title: Traffic camera ordinance (AVIS)
denver/16.summary: Council worked on changes to the ordinance for the automated vehicle identification system, the city's photo traffic enforcement cameras.

denver/17.title: Council positions on Amendments 81 and 82
denver/17.summary: Council took up a proclamation opposing state ballot Amendment 81 on law enforcement and discussed Amendment 82 on a constitutional right to buy and sell natural gas.

denver/18.title: Limits on spending dedicated taxes on alcohol and perks
denver/18.summary: Council advanced bills barring Caring for Denver, Denver Preschool Program and college affordability tax money from being spent on alcohol, staff wellness programs and similar administrative costs.

denver/19.title: East Colfax sidewalk land acquisition
denver/19.summary: Council moved an ordinance letting the city buy or condemn land to add sidewalks where none exist along East Colfax in District 8.

denver/20.title: Entertainment license overhaul
denver/20.summary: Council updated the city code for entertainment licenses, including application and license fees.

denver/21.title: Filling an at-large council seat
denver/21.summary: A special meeting declared a vacancy in one of the two at-large council seats.

sources.body: Special Meeting Of The City Council

denver/22.title: ShotSpotter contract cut
denver/22.summary: Council cut about $147,000 from the SoundThinking (ShotSpotter) gunshot detection contract.

erie/0.title: Town mineral rights and the Draco oil and gas pad
erie/0.summary: After SM Energy backed out of buying town-owned mineral rights for its Draco drilling project, council repealed the sale ordinance and discussed whether to lease the minerals instead and what role the town should play in the state drilling permit process.

erie/1.title: New oil and gas rules and fees
erie/1.summary: The planning commission reviewed a rewrite of the town's oil and gas regulations covering per-well fees, legacy wells, noise, air quality, inspections and notification, with a resident urging higher inspection fees.

erie/2.title: 2027 budget cuts amid falling revenue
erie/2.summary: With sales tax growth under 2% and use tax and building permits down more than 40%, staff built a leaner 2027 budget with few new positions; advisory boards were told to cut their budgets, and hearings were set for October 27 and November 10.

erie/3.title: Page property open space rezoning
erie/3.summary: The open space board recommended rezoning land on the Page property west of the Cottonwood Extension Ditch as Reserved Open Space, which needs voter approval to ever sell or rezone, ahead of a council discussion set for November 10.
erie/3.where: Page property, near Reliance Park and CR 1.5

sources.body: Open Space and Trails Advisory Board
Open Space and Trails Advisory Board

erie/4.title: Protecting open space through zoning
erie/4.summary: The planning commission and open space board held a joint session on how open space is zoned, the Reserved Open Space district, the land acquisition strategy and how the open space board reviews development.

sources.body: Open Space and Trails Advisory Board
Open Space and Trails Advisory Board

erie/5.title: Vista Ridge golf course and Vista Reserve development
erie/5.summary: The planning commission and council took up two amendments to the Vista Ridge planned development, including changes for the golf course and the Vista Reserve preliminary plat.

erie/6.title: Short-term rental rules
erie/6.summary: The planning commission and council held hearings on adding a short-term rental chapter to the town's development code.

erie/7.title: Erie Municipal Airport noise, hangars and fees
erie/7.summary: Residents complained about early-morning touch-and-go flights, while the airport board worked on hangar development, through-the-fence fees and a possible charter change to allow longer land leases, and council got a hangar development update.

erie/8.title: Hiring a new town manager
erie/8.summary: After 60 applications and interviews, council appointed Kelli Johnson as town manager starting January 4, 2027.

erie/9.title: Colliers Hill urban renewal tax increment
erie/9.summary: The urban renewal authority and council approved tax increment agreements for the Colliers Hill area, including a Weld County amendment that drops a requirement to spend some revenue on Weld County Road 5 and allows parks and recreation projects.

erie/10.title: Downtown Briggs Street redevelopment
erie/10.summary: The urban renewal authority paid for downtown infrastructure and design work and took up a development agreement for 150 Briggs Street, while council approved sidewalk patio licenses for businesses on Briggs Street.

erie/11.title: Erie Lake Dam seepage repairs
erie/11.summary: Council amended the design and construction contracts for the project to fix seepage at the Erie Lake dam.

erie/12.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing commitment
erie/12.summary: The town is asking the state to cut its Proposition 123 affordable housing requirement to 30 units, and planners discussed how the commitment will shape the development code update.

erie/13.title: Lodging tax and sales tax ballot measures
erie/13.summary: Two ballot measures are coming, a proposed 3.5% lodging tax tied to the Sundance Film Festival and a proposed sales tax increase.

sources.body: Open Space and Trails Advisory Board

erie/14.title: Coal Creek rezoning and stream restoration
erie/14.summary: The planning commission heard a rezoning of the Coal Creek property, and council authorized buying land for the County Line Road and Coal Creek stream restoration project.

erie/15.title: Water purchases and conservation
erie/15.summary: Council approved buying Colorado-Big Thompson water units, a home water audit program with Boulder County, and heard a presentation on Northern Water's NISP reservoir project.

erie/16.title: Flock cameras and security
erie/16.summary: Council met in executive session on security arrangements and Flock Safety license plate camera technology.

glendale/0.title: Xcel franchise ballot question
glendale/0.summary: Council took up a resolution on ballot question 2B, which would grant Xcel Energy a new franchise in Glendale.

glendale/1.title: 2027 budget and tax levy
glendale/1.summary: Council introduced ordinances adopting the 2027 budget and setting the property tax levy, followed by a budget update.

glendale/2.title: Four Mile project
glendale/2.summary: Council met in executive session for legal advice on the Four Mile project.

glendale/3.title: Clubhouse entertainment liquor license
glendale/3.summary: Council held a public hearing on a new entertainment facility liquor license for a clubhouse on South Colorado Boulevard.

glendale/4.title: Community events planning
glendale/4.summary: Volunteer teams reported on the car show, Music on the Plaza and Get to Know Glendale events.

longmont/0.title: Vance Brand Airport noise and future
longmont/0.summary: The city held a town hall on what it can and cannot legally do about airport noise, and council held a vision session on the airport's future, governance and rebuilding trust with neighbors.
longmont/0.where: Vance Brand Municipal Airport, 229 Airport Rd

sources.body: Town Hall: What the City Can and Cannot Do About Airport Noise

longmont/1.title: First and Main urban renewal and downtown tax increment deals
longmont/1.summary: The urban renewal authority approved tax increment revenue agreements with the city, Boulder County, Northern Water, St. Vrain Valley Schools and the Downtown Development Authority for the 1st and Main redevelopment area, which also came up at a joint meeting with county commissioners.

sources.body: City Council Joint Meeting with Boulder County Commissioners

longmont/2.title: Trash, compost and sanitation rates
longmont/2.summary: Council discussed lining up waste and compost rates with city policy goals and asked the Sustainability Advisory Board for feedback on the sanitation rate structure.

longmont/3.title: Water supply, drought and Ralph Price Reservoir
longmont/3.summary: The Water Board weighed a one-year water exchange with the St. Vrain and Left Hand Water Conservancy District, whose supply could run out by 2028 in continued drought, reviewed how Ralph Price Reservoir is managed, and heard about the Dry Creek Fire near Button Rock.
longmont/3.where: Button Rock Preserve / Ralph Price Reservoir

longmont/4.title: Affordable housing and the inclusionary housing fee
longmont/4.summary: The housing board reviewed the inclusionary housing ordinance, which requires 12% affordable units or a fee instead, as part of a housing needs update, and housing funding and demand for for-sale homes came up with county commissioners and the school board.

sources.body: City Council Joint Meeting with the Board of Education
City Council Joint Meeting with Boulder County Commissioners
Housing and Human Service Advisory Board

longmont/5.title: Human services funding hearings
longmont/5.summary: The Housing and Human Service Advisory Board set a scoring threshold and held weekly hearings with nonprofits applying for city human services funding.

longmont/6.title: Show cause hearing for 333 Main Street liquor license
longmont/6.summary: The licensing authority scheduled a show cause hearing on a bar at 333 Main Street over rowdiness, noise, disturbances and open container violations.

sources.body: Local Licensing Authority- CONTINUED TO DATE TBD

longmont/7.title: Platte River Power and clean energy goals
longmont/7.summary: Platte River Power Authority told the Sustainability Advisory Board it cannot reach 100% noncarbon power by 2030 and is starting a new resource plan, and the board began work on the 2027 sustainability tax.

longmont/8.title: City flag redesign
longmont/8.summary: A selection panel and the Art in Public Places Commission worked through submissions for a new official Longmont flag.

sources.body: City of Longmont Official City Flag Redesign Selection Panel Meeting

longmont/9.title: Automated checkout workforce impact fee
longmont/9.summary: Council members discussed a possible fee on stores that replace cashiers with automated checkout.

longmont/10.title: New homes at 10930 Airport Road
longmont/10.summary: A neighborhood meeting covered a proposal for new single-family homes at 10930 Airport Road that would need a comprehensive plan amendment, rezoning and subdivision.

longmont/11.title: Front Range Passenger Rail
longmont/11.summary: The urban renewal authority considered a letter of support for Front Range Passenger Rail.

longmont/12.title: Property tax burden
longmont/12.summary: At its legislative dinner, council raised the gap between the property taxes residents pay and what cities receive.

louisville/0.title: Inclusionary housing ordinance update
louisville/0.summary: Council rewrote the inclusionary housing rules that require affordable units in new development, drawing letters from Strong Towns Louisville and residents asking for small-project exemptions and by-right incentives, before a final hearing in September.

louisville/1.title: Golf course fees and the Coal Creek Golf Fund deficit
louisville/1.summary: With the golf fund's costs projected to outrun green fees, the recreation board modeled fee increases, heard golfers worried about losing the course's community culture, and sent 2027 fee and pass recommendations to council.

louisville/2.title: 2027-2028 budget and operating deficit
louisville/2.summary: Council worked through a "transitionary" budget with costs growing faster than revenue, an operating deficit, service level cuts such as cancelled event sponsorships, a refined six-year capital plan, and a final budget hearing on October 20.

louisville/3.title: Centennial Valley residential development plan
louisville/3.summary: Council and its boards held hearings on amending the Centennial Valley general development plan to allow housing that could grow Louisville's housing by 12%, with residents arguing the parks, trails and open space in the plan are too small.

louisville/4.title: AdventHealth hospital and helipad at Redtail Ridge
louisville/4.summary: Council took up the planned development and a special review use for a helicopter pad at the AdventHealth (Avista) hospital at Redtail Ridge, with questions about exemptions from LEED and solar requirements.

louisville/5.title: Delo Boom 135-unit development
louisville/5.summary: The planning commission reviewed the final plans for 135 homes and a small commercial space at 1390 Cannon Street and 1301 Courtesy Road, with supporters citing the need for attainable housing and a Delo resident warning of a parking shortfall.

louisville/6.title: Open space, parks and trails long-range plan
louisville/6.summary: Boards and council reviewed the draft PROS guidebook and trails plan, with the open space group LOSA objecting to land classifications and trails it says conflict with the city charter's open space protections.

louisville/7.title: Sustainability funding, bag tax and electrification rebates
louisville/7.summary: The sustainability board and council discussed a sustainability tax, renegotiating the Xcel franchise, using bag tax money, water conservation in a snowmelt-dependent system and new home electrification and heat pump rebates.

louisville/8.title: Marshall Fire five-year remembrance
louisville/8.summary: Council reviewed survey results on a Marshall Fire five-year remembrance, with remembrance funds going toward Superior's memorial project.

louisville/9.title: Fire Smart Louisville wildfire program
louisville/9.summary: Council funded Fire Smart Louisville, a volunteer effort with the Boulder Watershed Collective to help neighborhoods reduce wildfire risk, and approved a $100,000 agreement with the collective.

louisville/10.title: Comprehensive plan and development code update
louisville/10.summary: The planning commission reviewed the new comprehensive plan's growth projections and the city launched a development code rewrite with state grant money, as residents raised concerns about growth, traffic, water, wildfire evacuation and community character.

louisville/11.title: Affordable housing strategy and Prop 123
louisville/11.summary: Council heard a housing strategic framework from Trestle Strategy Group, reviewed a concept for affordable senior housing on Centennial Drive, and set expedited review for affordable projects and a state Prop 123 commitment.

louisville/12.title: Historic preservation tax ballot measure and landmarks
louisville/12.summary: Council took a position on the November historic preservation tax measure and designated landmarks including the Caranci House at 1101 Main and the Giorzelli House, with grants for the James House, Mudrock House and the grain elevator at 540 County Road.
louisville/12.where: 1101 Main St, 700 Pine St, 613 Grant Ave, 741 Jefferson Ave

louisville/13.title: Grain Elevator and Grain Yard redevelopment
louisville/13.summary: The Revitalization Commission worked on a tax increment financing agreement for the Grain Elevator and facade and property improvement grants for the Grain Yard.

louisville/14.title: Front and Center construction impacts downtown
louisville/14.summary: Business owners raised worries that the Front and Center construction project will hurt Street Fair and Front Street businesses, and commissioners discussed construction impact support grants.

louisville/15.title: Trash, recycling and compost rate increases
louisville/15.summary: Council set new refuse, recycling and compost collection fees effective September 1, with questions about why recycling and compost rates rose.

louisville/16.title: Utility rates for 2027
louisville/16.summary: A revised 2027 water and sewer rate presentation was delayed and then discussed, and the northeast water loop project was pulled from the budget after rate talks.

louisville/17.title: Business incentives for Infleqtion and Arsenal Health
louisville/17.summary: Council approved business assistance agreements worth $281,114 for Infleqtion Quantum and $208,400 for Arsenal Health.

louisville/18.title: City land deals at Empire Road, 1155 Pine Street and Gateway open space
louisville/18.summary: Council approved buying land at 1501 Empire Road, extended a lease-purchase at 1155 Pine Street, and approved buying the Gateway open space property.
louisville/18.where: 1501 Empire Rd, 1155 Pine St, Gateway open space

louisville/19.title: Bocce court and Community Park upkeep
louisville/19.summary: Residents asked for better upkeep of the bocce courts at Memory Square and Community Park, and boards pushed for shade structures and flower bed improvements at Community Park.

louisville/20.title: Prairie dogs on open space
louisville/20.summary: Residents asked the open space board to deal with prairie dogs moving into neighborhoods near open space.

superior/0.title: Marshall Fire Remembrance and five-year anniversary
superior/0.summary: The town is designing a Marshall Fire Remembrance with a gathering place and pet memorial, setting up fundraising through Colorado Gives with $25,000 committed by Louisville, and planning a five-year anniversary resilience celebration on December 18.

sources.body: Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)
Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)

superior/1.title: 2027 budget and property tax levy
superior/1.summary: Council held a series of budget review sessions on the 2027 budget and five-year plan, with sales tax flat and vehicle use tax down, then set a public hearing to adopt the budget, fees and property tax levy along with the metro district and urban renewal budgets.

superior/2.title: Zaharias property development at 7500 S 88th Street
superior/2.summary: Garrett Companies sought a 25th amendment to the Rock Creek Ranch planned development for the Zaharias property, with residents speaking at the planning commission hearing before it went to council.

superior/3.title: Pirate Park playground renovation
superior/3.summary: Council approved a design-build contract with Altitude Recreation to rebuild the Pirate Park playground, and the parks committee and council got regular progress updates.

superior/4.title: Water conservation and turf reduction
superior/4.summary: The town drafted a waterwise landscape roadmap and a tool for ranking non-functional turf to remove, gathered resident input on Shape Superior, and amended its Northern Water supply allotment.

superior/5.title: Prairie dog and wildlife management plans
superior/5.summary: The open space committee worked on a prairie dog management plan covering relocation and conflicts, a broader town wildlife plan, and balancing wildfire mitigation with habitat.

superior/6.title: Coyote Ridge trail recommendations
superior/6.summary: A consultant presented recommended trail projects for Coyote Ridge open space, to be priced and scheduled once staff sign off.

superior/7.title: Adopting the 2024 International Fire Code
superior/7.summary: Council adopted the 2024 International Fire Code after a hearing continued from August, with the Mountain View Fire Protection District presenting.

superior/8.title: Boulder County early childhood mill levy
superior/8.summary: Council passed a resolution supporting the Boulder County ballot measure to raise the property tax for early childhood care and education, after discussing the county's child care investment initiative.

superior/9.title: 88th Street bike and pedestrian improvements
superior/9.summary: Council approved an agreement with CDOT for bicycle and pedestrian improvements along 88th Street.

superior/10.title: Trash, recycling and electric garbage trucks
superior/10.summary: Republic Services briefed council on contamination, blocked containers and its electric collection trucks, as the town looks at a future single-hauler contract and apartment recycling and composting.

superior/11.title: Rock Creek Parkway, Community Center and pool construction
superior/11.summary: Council received construction updates on Rock Creek Parkway, the community center and the north and south pools.
superior/11.where: Rock Creek Parkway, Superior Community Center
